hero.tagline: The full MitID flow for a building permit in 60 seconds. Open source on bare Drupal 11. No licence fees, no per-form charges.

comparison.heading: What you get that proprietary alternatives don't offer
comparison.lead: Most workflow platforms in the Danish municipal market are closed, licence-based and vendor-hosted. Here's how we differ:

row2.title: Visual modeler
row2.us: Open it, read it, change it yourself in the visual modeler

row3.title: Hosting
row3.us: Own server or EU VPS, ideally Denmark - you own the data and the location

row4.title: Pricing model
row4.us: Free software. You only pay for hosting and optional consulting.
row4.them: Annual licence plus a fee per submitted form or case

comparison.footnote: The proprietary alternatives solve their problem just fine. We solve it in a way you can maintain yourself, without licence costs that scale with case volume.

hub.heading: Try ÅbenForms
hub.lead: We do not ask for what we already know.
hub.body: Every demo is a real self-service flow: you log in with a mock MitID, we fetch what the municipality already holds in its registers, and you only type what only you know. Then the case runs and the decision lands in Digital Post. Every step shows which register we asked, on which legal basis, and whether the rail is live or demo.
hub.comingBody: This scenario is on its way. Building permit can be tried now.
hub.offline: The demo runs locally with a mock MitID. Book a walkthrough via Contact.
hub.honestBody: Rails marked DEMO (e.g. CPR Family+ and eIndkomst) run against test data. LIVE-READY means the code is ready for the real service agreement. LIVE runs against a real source. The badges are the same as on the readiness board.

commentary.login: The frontend sends you to /mitid/login. Drupal creates state, nonce and a PKCE challenge and sends you to the identity provider. Back on /auth/callback we exchange the code for a session.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/[form]?session=[id] runs the register lookups the flow would run and returns every value with source, contract, legal basis and audit number. The CPR always arrives masked from the server.
commentary.form: Only what the registers do not know is asked for. Choices from list sources (child, case) travel with the application.
commentary.workflow: POST to /api/webform/[form]/submit runs the ECA flow synchronously and returns every step. The identity gate checks the session on the server.
commentary.letter: GET /api/digital-post/recent looks up the Digital Post log for your session. In production this is an SF1601 call to NgDP.

merudgifter.story: Freja applies for coverage of extra expenses for Emil. Children and income are fetched; she only writes about the need.

fields.funktionsnedsaettelseHint: For example the diagnosis and which extra expenses it causes day to day.
fields.maanedligMerudgiftHint: In the demo the threshold is 1,000 DKK/month: from 1,000 DKK the application is granted, below 1,000 DKK it ends in a refusal with appeal guidance.

validation.maanedligMerudgift: Enter the monthly extra expenses in DKK

medhold.heading: Granted: the extra expenses are covered
medhold.body: The amount is at least 1,000 DKK/month, so the flow granted the application, sent the decision letter and closed the case via SF2900.

afslag.heading: Refusal with appeal guidance
afslag.body: The amount is below 1,000 DKK/month. The flow ran the consultation of the party, refused the application, sent the letter with appeal guidance and started a 4-week appeal deadline.

neutral.heading: The decision has been sent
neutral.body: The decision letter is in Digital Post below.

commentary.login: The MitID login gives the municipality your CPR number. It only reaches the browser masked and is filled in on the server at submission.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/merudgifter fetches your children from CPR Family+ (SF6006, demo) and the household income from eIndkomst (demo). Every lookup is logged with its legal basis: Social Services Act section 41, Public Administration Act section 7, GDPR art. 6(1)(e).
commentary.form: Only what the registers do not know: the child's disability and the monthly extra expenses. The amount drives the decision in the demo: 1,000 DKK/month or more is granted, less gives consultation and a refusal.
commentary.workflow: The ECA flow opens and journals the case, fetches the income and branches on the amount: a grant is closed via SF2900, a refusal goes through consultation of the party and starts an appeal deadline.
commentary.letter: The decision letter is sent to Digital Post (simulated). On a refusal it carries appeal guidance, and the appeal deadline has started on the case.

commentary.title: What's happening behind the scenes
commentary.auth: The frontend redirects to /mitid/login. Drupal generates state + nonce + PKCE challenge and forwards you to Keycloak.
commentary.form: We fetch /mitid/session/{id} and pre-fill the form with id_token claims. CPR is shown masked in the UI.
commentary.workflow: POST to /api/webform/building_permit/submit runs the entire ECA flow synchronously and returns workflow.steps in the same response.
commentary.inbox: GET /api/digital-post/recent looks up aabenforms_digital_post_log by SHA-256 of your session CPR. The letter body is sanitised server-side.

page.title: Cookies on ÅbenForms
page.lead: See which cookies ÅbenForms sets in your browser, what they are for, and how to change your choice.
page.whatBody: A cookie is a small text file stored in your browser so the solution can remember something from one page view to the next, such as your language choice. A cookie cannot spread viruses or read other files on your computer.
page.listIntro: ÅbenForms currently sets only two cookies. Both are necessary for the solution to work, and neither is shared with anyone.
page.i18nPurpose: Remembers whether you chose Danish or English, so you get the same language next time.
page.consentPurpose: Remembers your answer to the cookie banner (accepted or rejected), so you are not asked again.
page.necessaryHeading: Necessary cookies do not require consent
page.necessaryBody: Necessary cookies are the ones the solution needs to remember your own choices. We may set them without asking first, and they are not used to follow you across websites.
page.mitidHeading: Your MitID login is not a cookie
page.mitidBody: When you log in with MitID, the server keeps track of your session. Your browser only stores a session id in its local storage (not in a cookie), and it is deleted when you log off or the session expires.
page.statsBody: We currently set no statistics cookies and load no third-party scripts. If we add statistics later, they are only enabled if you accepted cookies in the banner, and we update this page first.
page.choiceRejected: You have said no thanks to cookies.
page.choiceNone: You have not made a choice yet. The banner is shown at the bottom of the page.
page.resetDone: Your choice has been cleared. The banner is shown again at the bottom of the page so you can choose anew.
